body: I also noticed that if you use `_process` in RigidBody connected to PinJoint3D, then RigidBodydoesn't move at all.

Hopefully this helps with debugging this. I'm currently on Godot 4.4, and I'm working on a local multiplayer game in which I pause the scene tree while procedurally generating a layout, and then I unpause when a match starts. If I instantiate a PinJoint2D while the scene tree is paused, and then unpause it, the joint will not affix two bodies. My current workaround is to emit an event after the scene tree is unpaused, which I respond to by instantiating the joint.

Maybe it should be `PROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLE` besides `PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED`?
I tried first `pausable` then switch to `inherit`, the pinJoint worked properly.

---

Edit: 2025-09-29

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp#L249C1-L249C54

`disable` caused `body_set_space()`, and `body->clear_constraint_list();`

So set `disable` caused losing `constraints`.

I think this is a interested un-completed feature. When disabled, we can control the physics behavior, either lose physics to drop without collisions, keep stay, or keep active without change. But this feature seems didn't implement completely. I leaves this clue for followers who want to go further.

I don't really get `disable_mode`, as it seems to always be its default header value: `DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE`. As @xuhuisheng said, it seems to be a feature that is not really finished / used.

But even without using another `disable_mode`, I don't think `DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE` should remove constraints, only remove the body from the space.

Simply removing the joint clears solves the problem, but constraints would reference a body that's temporarily not in any space, which could be problematic during the physics step if the body is accessed.
It would also be possible to re-add joints when enabling, but then the body should have references to its joints, or joints should listen for the enable signal.

I see these 3 possible solutions:
1: Don't clear constraints when disabling space
2: Iterate through body joints when a body changes space to re-add their constraints
3: Have joints listen to body enable to re-add their constraint

I have also confirmed this error and the cause @xuhuisheng found.

In addition to being a bug, it seems a significant architectural error to use set_space(0) and then set_space(space) to 'disable' something. 

set_space() is a PhysicsServer function, and the node is using it in a counter-intuitive way. Even if we got Godot working, how many physics engines would implement set_space() the way that is required here.

So I would add two more solutions because of the external engine problem:
1. Add a 'disable' function to the PhysicsServer for Bodies so that each Physics engine can implement it in a way that works.
2. Deprecate this whole disable_mode feature.

I would favour #2. Deprecating it may draw out anyone who is actually using it, and it prevents us supporting code that can't work (because of external engines).

Then if the functionality is needed, we are free to do it properly by adding body disable functionality to the Physics Server. 

We could also then consider presenting it to the user differently. It doesn't seem ideal that CollisionObject2D is declaring flags and documenting behaviour specific to only some of its base classes. It shouldn't be referring to 'simulation' and 'DISABLE_MODE_MAKE_STATIC'. This may be practically necessary, but ideally these simulation concepts should begin with PhysicsBody2D, not CollisionObject2D.

Worth adding another technicality. 2D Joints can't easily be re-created unless you move the RigidBodies back to their resting pose which eliminates the option of recreating them (you can recreate them within godot_physics_2d, but not via the PhysicsServer as would be necessary here):

[Reparenting joints with RigidBody2D introduces jarring offset #105230](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105230)

This is one of the trivial but problematic book keeping issues that I want to fix with this (or something similar):

[GenericJoint2D interface to unlock modern 2D Physics joint functionality #15126](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15126)
